question: Tuberculosis: what are the latest WHO figures, for the most recent year reported? How many people fell ill worldwide, how many died, and what share of treated people are cured? Answer with precise figures, the year they refer to, and cite your sources (title, year, URL).
answer:
The latest consolidated WHO figures are for **2023**, published in the **WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2024**:

* **Fell ill worldwide in 2023: 10.8 million people**
> including 6.0 million men, 3.6 million women and 1.3 million children, with TB present in all countries and age groups.

* **Died worldwide in 2023: 1.25 million people**
> including 1.09 million HIV-negative people and 161,000 people with HIV. TB was again the leading cause of death from a single infectious agent in 2023, ahead of COVID-19.

* **Share of treated people successfully treated / cured: 88%**
> treatment success rate of 88% among people enrolled on drug-susceptible TB treatment in the 2022 cohort. 8.2 million people were newly diagnosed and treated in 2023, up from 7.5 million in 2022.

Sources:
- WHO, Global tuberculosis report 2024, 2024, https://www.who.int/teams/global-tuberculosis-programme/tb-reports/global-tuberculosis-report-2024
- WHO, Tuberculosis Fact Sheet / Global tuberculosis report 2024 news release 29 Oct 2024, 2024, https://www.who.int/news/item/29-10-2024-tuberculosis-resurges-as-top-infectious-disease-killer
